data.name: Sudhira
data.gender_notes: Sudhira is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is pure and good, has been cleansed of all impurities. The name Sudhira carries the meaning “Pure, Good, Cleansed” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada. Parents who choose Sudhira usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, good, cleansed and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the purification of the mind and soul, leading to wisdom and enlightenment.
data.etymology: Sudhira belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pure, Good, Cleansed.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sudhira total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_sanskrit.name: सुधिर
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: सु (su) meaning good, virtuous, pure. धिर (dhira) meaning auspicious, strength, power. The name Sudhira is derived from the Sanskrit word सुधिर (sudhira), which is a combination of the words सु (su) and धिर (dhira).

data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, the name "Sudhira" holds immense significance for those on the path of self-realization and spiritual growth. It serves as a constant reminder of the importance of purifying the mind, body, and spirit to achieve inner peace and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sudhira: Purity and Enlightenment. This name signifies the inner journey towards clarity, knowledge, and illumination, much like the purifying effect of clean water, or the enlightening wisdom of a guru.

historical_references.reference: Sudhira was a celebrated sage and a disciple of the great sage Vyasa. He is known for his profound wisdom and is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures including the Mahabharata and the Puranas.

Sudhira was also a prominent king of the Vangatas, a sub-tribe of the Andhra dynasty, in the 2nd century CE. He is known for his military prowess and is noted for his victories against the Chalukyas and the Satavahanas.
